content: LLM tool-use for NL→constraint editing uses structured function/tool schemas. The LLM receives a JSON schema for each tool (name, parameters, types) and emits a typed tool call when the user writes natural language. MeetMate (arxiv 2312.06908) implemented 5 constraint actions (AddConstraint, ModifyConstraint, RemoveConstraint, ListConstraints, GetSuggestions) against a CP meeting scheduler via this exact pattern. OptiMUS and ConstraintLLM decompose NL→constraint into stages: intent classification, entity extraction, schema validation, then solver injection. The canonical flow is: NL input → LLM emits tool call JSON → application validates IDs/params → applies to solver → re-solves.
